attested.notes: Full humanise re-read against Parts C, D and E. Part E classification cut the performance-class lines: the invented Friday call before a CVL, the 2019 shop lease and its three-year lag, 'they almost never do', 'stricter than most guides admit', 'that is where you start', 'that changes the sums', 'the awkward version of this'. Unsupported typical-outcome quantifiers replaced with defensible caseload observation or with the mechanism ('most of our compulsory-stage calls', 'directors most often mis-read', 'anything quoted to us'). Repeated-device scan: the contrastive 'X, not Y' shape ran 13 times in running prose and is now 5, three of those in list or disclosure text; two verbatim echoes removed ('the same first question we ask when a director calls', 'five minutes, no obligation, no follow-up'). Derived insight strengthened where a line only summarised: dissolution removes the debtor rather than the debt, a liquidator takes control either way so a CVL buys timing and choice, the Gazette notice is the only warning and nobody sends a copy, rescue turns on whether the trade funds the arrangement, the MVL fee compares against the tax difference and not the filing fee, three separate clocks run on closure. Two stranger reads run with a fresh agent that had no drafting context. The first found the real fault: the page pivoted on 'solvent' and never defined it, and the six option notes duplicated the table below them, which was the reader's stated tab-close point. Solvency is now defined in the first sentence and the six notes carry the deciding factor instead of restating the grid. The second read found no fabricated reader context, no tab-close point, and the reader could restate the page's advice unprompted; its three remaining points were fixed (members glossed as shareholders, capital-versus-income given its consequence, 'standard route' and the either-way control claim grounded). One point from the second read is NOT fixed and is left open honestly: the reader wants a practitioner fee figure to decide on and the page gives none. Fee figures are governed centrally and are case-specific, so inventing a range here would be worse than the gap. Check 04 we-density dipped under the floor after the P-class cuts; it was restored with genuine practitioner voice in the sections that lacked it (what directors ask us once HMRC objects, what we ask about at the first conversation on a redundancy claim, the assets we see left behind in a dissolved company) rather than by padding hollow 'we'. Paragraph splitting brought every body paragraph under 400 chars, over-long count 9 to 0. Facts, figures, headings, callouts and links unchanged apart from adding the gov.uk BADR link inline to the 18% figure, a source already cited on the page. Note for the next session: committing this work puts the draft at 4 commits since the redraft baseline, so the next voice record will require a genuine fresh redraft of the weak sections rather than another patch.
